LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 6.3.1 FUTURE TIME (WILL/SHALL)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall), part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How would you talk about things that will happen tomorrow or later?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. words that express identify future time/actions for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use ‘will’/’shall’ to talk about future time/events,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. value the role of ‘will’ and ‘shall’ in communicating future time/intentions. • Learners are guided to recognise sentences with words that express future time from a text. • Learners are guided to talk about what they plan to do after school to express future time. • Learners are guided to ask and answer questions using words that express future time with peers. • Learners are guided to sing a song/rhyme using ‘will’ and ‘shall’. • Learners are guided to listen to story, poem or conversation read by the teacher and respond to questions using ‘will’/’shall’. How would you talk about things that will happen tomorrow or later?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Teamwork is enhanced as the learner actively participates in question and answer activity with peers using

‘shall’/’will’.

Values:
Responsibility is developed as the learner takes up roles in question and answer activity with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is boosted as they use will/shall effectively in communication.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner links the concept of future time to learning of similar concept in Indigenous and Kiswahili Language Activities.
